questions.p: were the 100+ vendors on the courts, between them, or in other spaces? Did nets come down? What did Peak charge, and is 2027 booked? The answers settle most of the questions below.
are the posts fixed in the concrete, or can nets come down for an event? How long does it take, and who does it?
can booths, pipe and drape, carpet, pallet jacks or vehicles go on the coated court surface? Are there weight or tape rules?
is there a dock or a large freight door, and where? How do exhibitors get stock to the upper level? Is there an elevator?
what is the fire-code occupancy for each level? What do promoters need from the fire marshal or Pikes Peak Regional Building for booth layouts?
does the lease limit event types (gun shows were raised), signage, hours, alcohol, or after-hours use of the lot? How many parking spaces sit near the Jamboree Drive entrance?
what is the booth power capacity? Can outside caterers come in, or only the Kitchen add-on? Is alcohol allowed, and under whose licence?
which days could Peak close one level, or the whole building, without hurting members? Multi-day sales (consignment, gift shows) need 3-5 days including set-up.
what is the day rate for a full buyout or a single level, versus the published $40/court/hour? What deposit and insurance certificate does Peak require from promoters?
is groupevents@peakpickleball.us the right inbox for promoters, and who answers it?
